newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico moves to further eradicate cattle diseases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico moves to further eradicate cattle diseases.

text.p: Mexico's Agriculture Ministry said Wednesday that five regions had been earmarked for a new drive to eradicate bovine tubercolosis and brucellosis in cattle.

In a statement, the ministry said the states of Chihuahua, Nuevo Leon, Durango and Yucatan and the northern part of Sinaloa have been designated as the new areas. Sonora state was declared free of the diseases last year.
The drive to eradicate the diseases includes cattle movement controls and vaccinations. Areas declared free of the killer diseases are allowed to export cattle under accords with the United States.
The ministry said the Binational Commission for Bovine Tubercolosis and Brucellosis Cooperation agreed the new drive at the annual meeting of the National Livestock Confederation.
